## Scene 1: The Empty Roof

It was the summer of 1994, the kind that made tar roads soft and dogs move slowly. On the crumbling terrace of Shivam Bhavan in Pune, Kauwa the crow sat very still, watching the street below. A cycle-rickshaw, three Ambassadors, and one brand-new Maruti 800 crawled past. He had spotted a half-eaten vada pav sitting on the second-floor windowsill, unguarded, perfect.

[CROW_SAYS: ...]

## Scene 2: The Clever Cat

Billi was asleep on the warm ledge beneath the water tank, her striped tail curled around her like a coiled telephone cord. She had seen the vada pav appear at exactly 9 AM when the bai delivered it. She had been biding her time since then.

[CAT_SAYS: ...]

## Scene 3: The Dog Who Smelled Everything

Kutta had been sitting behind the neem tree at the gate of Shivam Bhavan since early morning. He was not as crafty as Billi, nor as quick as Kauwa. But in the entire mohalla, nobody had a nose like his.

[DOG_SAYS: ...]

## Scene 4: The Meeting Under the Peepal Tree

At noon, when the whole neighbourhood was asleep under the summer heat and the cable TV was showing nothing but test patterns and old Chitrahaar, all three slipped away and met under the big peepal tree near the Ganesh mandir.

[CROW_SAYS: ...]
[CAT_SAYS: ...]
[DOG_SAYS: ...]

## Scene 5: The Feast

By evening, all three were back on the terrace of Shivam Bhavan. Kauwa had the vada pav. Billi had found a whole bowl of malai. Kutta had somehow come into possession of two atta rotis. The last red sun of May melted slowly behind the water tower as they ate together without speaking, which is the nicest way to eat with friends.

[CROW_SAYS: ...]
